title: Microdemo bootstrapping playbook — jot
body:
Context / why this exists:
This is a lightweight checklist + hypothesis log for the "microdemo" onboarding flow idea we discussed in last product sync. Goal: get a new developer to a tiny, shareable working demo (1-2 API calls, visible results) in under 5 minutes, while collecting telemetry that helps us improve retention and reduce support friction.

What "microdemo" means here:
- A minimal, scaffolded example tailored to the user persona (quickstart dev, prototype builder).
- Consists of a single minimal project (JS/TS + curl) or a code playground embed that calls Redwood API, shows streaming tokens and cost estimate, and a tiny results panel (e.g., summarization or chat).
- No sign-up detours: can run with ephemeral demo key or sandboxed token (clear limits).

Primary hypotheses (measurable):
1) H1: Reducing first-run steps to <=5 will increase 7-day activation rate by 20% for trial signups.
   - Metric: percent of new signups that make one successful generation within 1 hour and again within 48 hours.
2) H2: Showing immediate cost transparency (per-request estimate) reduces support tickets about billing by 30%.
   - Metric: #billing-related support threads from new accounts in first 14 days.
3) H3: Exposing live token usage + latency in the demo increases adoption of batch/kv-cache features later.
   - Metric: fraction of demo users who enable caching/optimization flags in subsequent 30 days.

Minimum viable scope (MVP):
- A single condensed quickstart page + code embed for Node/curl (HTML + playground).
- Auto-provision ephemeral sandbox token with strict quotas and labeled telemetry (demo_flow:microdemo-v1).
- Visual widget: streaming output, tokens consumed, cost estimate, latency watermark.
- Telemetry backend tags: session_id, demo_token_id, entrypoint (docs/embed/console), events: click_run, api_success, api_error, copy_shortcode, share_demo.
- Analytics dashboard: simple cohort: by entrypoint, time-to-first-success, failure-rate, avg tokens.
- Short support doc and canned chat responses for common errors.

User stories (rough):
- As a new developer, I want to paste a snippet and see immediate output so I know the API works. Acceptance: run -> streaming text appears, tokens counter increments, no account billing popup.
- As a product manager, I want to see where users drop off so I can optimize the quickstart. Acceptance: dashboard shows funnel (page view -> run -> success -> share).
- As an engineer, I want demo calls instrumented with demo_token so we can identify anon usage and safely inspect sample traces. Acceptance: traces are tagged, privacy-preserving (no PII), and TTL-limited.

Implementation notes / rough tech plan:
- Frontend: small static page in docs repo + embedded CodeMirror quick-run box; reuse existing streaming client. Keep dependencies small.
- Token service: extend internal dev-sandbox service to mint ephemeral demo tokens with tag demo_flow= microdemo-v1 and quota: 500 tokens per token / 10 requests max. Tokens auto-revoke after 24h.
- Telemetry: create one lightweight event schema (demo_event.v1) and a dataset/PII policy (no free-text logs saved; only hashes of inputs if needed). Aggregate pipeline to BigQuery for dashboards.
- SDK: snippet for Node and curl, and a tiny TypeScript example that wires up streaming into the embedded UI.
- Observability: add quick SLOs for demo infra (token mint latency, demo-run success rate) and alert on failure >5% for 1h.

Open questions / tradeoffs (note to self):
- Privacy: should we allow users to opt-out of telemetry per-demo? probably show a small checkbox and explain it helps debugging. But opt-out reduces sample quality.
- Security: ephemeral tokens might get scraped; ensure strict quotas and easy revocation. Consider IP white-listing from embed host.
- Cost: demo usage could be gamed; start with very small token budgets. Monitor and burn-rate alarm.
- UX friction: streaming output is delightful but increases client complexity. MVP could use non-streaming then upgrade.

Draft onboarding funnel (text flow):
1) Landing (docs snippet or marketing landing) -> click "Try a microdemo" -> open sandbox modal -> code editor + run button
2) Run displays streaming results + token + cost tile (left) + "Save as example" or "Share link" on success
3) If success, prompt: "Would you like to continue in your account?" with CTA to create an account or claim demo results.

Instrumentation: events to emit (minimal):
- demo_view (entrypoint, timestamp)
- demo_run_attempt (session_id, snippet_id, runtime_ms)
- demo_run_success (tokens, latency_ms, cost_estimate_cents)
- demo_run_error (error_code, retryable)
- demo_share (anonymous_id, share_token)
- demo_claim (user_id if claimed)

Rollout plan (alpha -> beta -> GA):
- alpha (internal + friends): cherry-picked infra + SRE guardrails, manual QA, 1 week of close monitoring.
- beta (open to new signups): expose in docs with banner; soft limit on total demo tokens/day. 2 weeks monitoring and optimize funnel.
- GA: promote in marketing if funnel tests positive; integrate with onboarding emails.

Success criteria (to move to next stage):
- Alpha -> Beta: demo run success rate >= 90% and no > P0 incidents.
- Beta -> GA: relative lift of activation metric >= 15% or demonstrable support reduction in billing questions.

Next steps (next 2 weeks):
- Draft the static quickstart page (me) — target: 3 days.
- Patch sandbox-token service for ephemeral token (Elliot) — target: 1 week.
- Initial dashboard and telemetry schema (Zara) — target: 1 week.
- Quick security review + quota thresholds (SRE) — request by EOD Thu.
- Prototype demo embed and internal alpha signups (small list) — aim to launch internal alpha by 2026-02-10.

Notes to self / tiny parking lot items:
- Think about lightweight "save example" that creates a permalink with tokenized claim flow.
- Consider embedding a tiny cost calculator that lets users toggle model size to see cost delta.
- Revisit streaming vs non-streaming decision after alpha telemetry.
- Draft short copy for banner + microcopy explaining ephemeral token behavior.

Quick scratch UX wire (words only):
[Header] Microdemo: Try Redwood in 2 clicks
[Editor] Paste example or choose sample (Summarize / Chat / Rewrite)
[Run] -> [Output streaming pane] [tokens | est cost | latency] [share/save]

---
Revision log:
- 2025-11-03 initial stub (Ava)
- 2025-11-12 added telemetry event list (Zara)
- 2025-12-02 trimmed scope for MVP (Elliot)
- 2026-02-20 updated rollout dates and success criteria (Ava)

Unresolved: which docs entrypoint yields the best lift? (marketing banner vs docs home). Put this on the weekly product experiment list.

End of jot.
